text:
For a period, Detroit looked like the better team at Ball Arena. The Red Wings out-chanced Colorado 0.95 to 0.72 in expected goals (the quality of their chances) in the first, and Mackenzie Blackwood was the reason it was still 0-0. By the end of the night he had stopped all 27 shots for his first shutout of the season, and the Avalanche had won 4-0 without ever really winning at even strength.

That is the detail worth sitting with. At even strength the Red Wings created more than Colorado did, 1.79 expected goals to 1.51. The game was decided on the power play, where the Avalanche went 3 for 5 and built 1.67 expected goals of their own while Detroit went 0 for 3. Martin Necas opened it at 9:46 of the second on a man-advantage chance worth 66 percent, and Nathan MacKinnon blasted a slap shot through on another power play less than three minutes later. Colorado took the second period 2.00 to 0.30 in chances, and our win probability model had them at 88 percent after MacKinnon scored.

Necas added a batted-in goal at even strength midway through the third, then set up Cale Makar's power-play wrister, a 4 percent look that probably shouldn't have gone in. Necas finished with two goals and two assists; Makar and MacKinnon had three points each. Our numbers say Colorado deserved to win 73 percent of the time, a fair reading of a team that was sharper when it mattered and disciplined enough to make Detroit pay for 19 penalty minutes.

Daniil Tarasov allowed four on 29 shots for the Red Wings, a bit worse than expected, and he is in the crease because John Gibson got hurt this week and Michal Postava was recalled on an emergency basis. That is the smaller of Detroit's problems. The bigger one hangs over everything: Dylan Larkin, the captain, is not with the team and wants out, and the headlines this week were about timelines and suitors, not hockey. Viktor Arvidsson has been a bright spot. A night like this, with the power play blanked and the even-strength edge wasted, shows how thin the margin is without Larkin.
headline: Blackwood blanks Detroit as Avs' power play does the rest
